failures.criterion: Acceptance 2 / the reviewer's round-1 finding on codegraph.go: two contenders that both judged one lease stale never both build — on the filesystem a pod's workspace actually lives on.
failures.evidence: The tree volume reuses inode numbers (measured: on /legion/workspaces, v9fs, a file removed and re-created at one path gets its inode back — `touch; stat; rm; touch; stat` → 95 → 95; the overlayfs under /tmp gives a new number) and os.SameFile compares device and inode alone, so takeOverWarmLease's guard `os.SameFile(stale, current)` matches the fresh lease the first contender created at the same path. Interleaving: B judges the lease stale; A takes it over (marker, remove, drop marker) and creates its fresh lease, which reuses the inode; B takes the marker, stats the path, reads A's live lease as the file it judged stale, removes it, and creates its own — both hold, both build. Shown two ways at 3a77eb10: (1) the implementer's own subtest `TestTwoContendersThatJudgedOneLeaseStaleCannotBothHoldIt/the_first_to_act_holds…` fails 3/3 with `A holds = true, B holds = true` when its TempDir is on the tree volume (`TMPDIR=<dir on /legion/workspaces> go test -run … ./internal/workspace/`) and passes on /tmp; (2) live, two real shims contending for a 5-minute-old lease on the tree volume: the fresh lease got the stale lease's inode in two of three runs (85313→85313, 100156→100156), the hazard window itself not hit in three runs. Red test, its own commit e0d55237, deterministic on any filesystem (the inode is pinned with a hard link): `cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 -run TestATakeoverLeavesAFreshLeaseThatReusedTheStaleOnesInode ./internal/workspace/` → `B took the lease over although A, acting first, holds a fresh lease at the path: two builds would run on one index`, 2/2 at 3a77eb10. The test accepts a takeover that leaves a fresh lease at the path whatever its inode (re-judge staleness by mtime under the marker, not identity), B skipping, the marker gone.

implementerProof.how: The stop-grace half held when driven independently at 3a77eb10 with the branch's `legion worker-shim --pod-safety --stop-grace 10s --warm-codegraph` (the flags launcherCommand now passes) wrapping the real Oh My Pi on a fresh clone: a group SIGTERM 8 s into the build → shim gone 0.12 s after, exit 143, lease released, the warm-up's end logged; with an agent stand-in that ignores SIGTERM → the agent killed at its 5 s grace, shim gone 5.39 s after the signal, exit 137, inside the 10 s stop grace, lease released. `--stop-grace 0s` is refused before any dial; the round-2 binary refuses the launcher's new flag outright. The lease half does not hold: the proof's interleaving test ran on /tmp in the implementer's pod (overlayfs, no inode reuse), so `removes the lease only while it is still the file judged stale` was measured on a filesystem where a fresh lease never looks like the stale one; on the tree volume, where the lease lives, the same test fails 3/3 (TMPDIR on /legion/workspaces) and my hard-link test fails deterministically everywhere.

observations: The fix direction for the failure is small: under the marker, re-judge whatever is at the path by mtime (older than warmLeaseStale → remove; fresh → leave) instead of, or in addition to, os.SameFile; a fresh lease is never the stale one whatever its inode. The marker and the one retry are right as they are.

Why the implementer's and reviewer's tests did not catch it: t.TempDir() is under /tmp, an overlayfs in these pods whose allocator hands out increasing inode numbers; the lease lives on the tree volume (v9fs over the issue's EBS volume), which reuses them at once. A test of a file-identity guard belongs on the filesystem the guard runs on, or pins the identity itself, as the new test does with a hard link.

Live contention on the tree volume (three runs, two shims, a 5-minute-old lease): one builder each time, both skip messages observed (`holds` and `is taking over`), inode reuse observed in two runs; the hazard window itself was not hit live, as expected for a microsecond race.

The stop-grace fix holds on the worst path: an agent ignoring SIGTERM is killed at 5 s and the shim is gone 5.39 s after the group signal with the lease released — 4.6 s inside the pod's default 10 s grace; the real Oh My Pi path is 0.12 s.

The round-2 binary (e865b2c1) refuses `--stop-grace`, so a daemon of this commit cannot start a shim from an image built before ad8329aa; the image probe's extensions=discovered mark does not express this (a pre-ad8329aa image of this branch would pass the probe and fail at the launcher's start). Pairing the daemon and the image is the operator's existing rule for this branch (build the image from the daemon's commit); noted, not a failure.
